item.title: FIFA to grant access to documents from scrapped World Cup sell-off plan
item.description: FIFA scrapped the $20 billion ‌World Cup sell-off plan earlier this summer only days after making it public.

item.title: Shah Rukh Khan at 61: The King who still cries in private
item.description: SRK was the outsider who took the roles nobody wanted, the orphan who turned loss into a refusal of victimhood, and the star whose most famous ritual was his wife’s idea. On his 61st birthday, Shah Rukh Khan is releasing a song, skipping the usual midnight balcony appearance, and asking the only question that still matters: can the audience that made him be assembled one more time?

item.title: “ART outlines steps Bangladesh needs to take to compete in the global economy”
item.description: “The agreement outlines it all in one key document — 36 pages available on the USTR website; it’s not a secret. And I encourage everybody to go out and read that agreement because it really does outline the way to grow the economic relationship.”

item.title: Bangladesh wins another gold at Asia Cup Archery
item.description: Abdur Rahman Alif, Sagar Islam and Abdulla Al Mohammad Rafi secured the title by defeating Kazakhstan 6–2 in set points in the final in Sulaymaniyah, Iraq, on Thursday.

item.title: “Bangladesh needs training, regulations to assess rooftop solar efficiency”
item.description: “Given the lack of available land in Bangladesh, rooftop solar is obviously one of the easiest ways to proceed. I think it is a matter of introducing training or regulations to assess the efficiency of existing installations. We could go back, identify the problems and upgrade those systems. That could have an immediate impact, alongside the rollout of new solutions.”

item.title: “Other countries can learn from Bangladesh on climate migration”
item.description: “Research only scratches the surface of lived realities. But from what people tell us, the messages for policy are fairly clear: human rights, agency, and empowering people to take their futures into their own hands, along with the crucial role of government in providing infrastructure and a good, democratic public space where civil society and the private sector can plan ahead.”

item.title: The classics, rewritten: Anne Carson wins the Nobel
item.description: The Swedish Academy praised Carson for creating new forms of contemporary literature through a playful dialogue with the classical tradition.

item.title: “Japanese companies want policy stability before committing to major investment”
item.description: “When Japanese companies make investment decisions, they require a high level of confidence. They’d like to see the situation regarding energy supply, infrastructure, customs clearance and taxation. Interest is different from an investment decision.”

item.title: ‘Hamlet’ reworked to give voice to displaced South Asian actors
item.description: Shahman Moishan’s play reimagines Rosencrantz and Guildenstern through the lens of South Asian history, with two characters confronting displacement, identity and history in contemporary Britain.

item.title: “Ziaur Rahman’s positive contributions made BNP popular with the public”
item.description: “The public has consistently viewed the standing, track record and principled stance of the proclaimer of independence President Ziaur Rahman, national leader Khaleda Zia and now Tarique Rahman favourably. None of them ever reneged on their commitments to the public.”

item.title: Disney’s ‘Toy Story 5’ fuels streaming business and merchandise sales for June quarter
item.description: CEO Josh D’Amaro, who took over in March, highlighted his strategy to invest in franchises like Toy Story to reach audiences outside the box office in a lengthy earnings letter to shareholders ​on Wednesday.

item.title: Puppetry pioneer, painter Mustafa Monwar passes away at 90
item.description: Mustafa Monwar earned national recognition for his creative children’s programming on the state broadcaster BTV, which shaped the childhoods of successive generations.
